subject: Eos-XS-2.7B adaptive pin & compatibility handoff for CloudScale POC
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eos-XS-2.7B: adaptive pin & compat checks for CloudScale POC

Jonas / team,

Quick context: CloudScale (contact: Sarah Park) wants to run a 6-week POC starting Nov 1 against a smaller, low-cost variant—we're proposing Eos-XS-2.7B (multitask) as the preferred candidate. They care about latency under 120ms p50 on our hosted offering and token-level cost.

Asks:
- Can we provisionally pin Eos-XS-2.7B (variant: eos-xs-mt-v1) for the CloudScale org for the duration of the POC?
- What compatibility checks do we need for tokenizer (BPE differences), KV-cache behavior, and quantization profiles?
- Any known model-serving risks (OOM, odd attention op) we should call out to sales/CS before go-live?

Attachments: eos-xs-specs.pdf, cloudscale-poc-brief.md (short doc for customer-facing SLA/targets).

Timing: We need a decision + basic rollout plan by EOD Thu (10/22) so sales can confirm on their end. If pinning is possible, we'd like a temporary pin until Nov 30 with telemetry hooks enabled.

Thanks — Avery

--
Avery Johnson
Product Manager, Model Intake
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Eos-XS-2.7B: adaptive pin & compat checks for CloudScale POC

Avery — thanks for the write-up and the spec. Quick replies inline.

> Can we provisionally pin Eos-XS-2.7B (variant: eos-xs-mt-v1) for the CloudScale org for the duration of the POC?
We can do a provisional, time-limited pin, but need sign-off on the rollout/rollback checklist and telemetry contract (token-level diffs, latency percentiles, and failure-rate SLO). Also need confirmation on whether CloudScale will accept a degraded fallback (e.g., fallback to eos-xs-mt-v1-quant if infra constrained).

> What compatibility checks do we need for tokenizer (BPE differences), KV-cache behavior, and quantization profiles?
Please run the checklist below and attach results:
- Tokenizer alignment: sample corpus (customer prompts) -> check token counts + special token handling.
- KV cache sizes: run a 512/1024 sequence simulation to estimate per-request KV footprint.
- Quantization: provide fp16 vs int8 output diff on 200-shot eval (we have a compat-check-template.csv you can use).

Dev / Priyom — can you take the technical lead on the compatibility runs and surface any non-trivial diff? If we see a >1% generation divergence on our eval prompts, we need product to OK acceptability.

Also request that CS draft a mutual action plan we can attach to the temporary pin (rollback window, Canary traffic %, contact list).

Jonas

Subject: Re: Eos-XS-2.7B: adaptive pin & compat checks for CloudScale POC

Taking this on. Initial plan and immediate blockers below.

What I'll run this week:
- Tokenizer alignment pass using CloudScale prompt set (will surface tokenization delta and edge-case tokens).
- Synthetic KV-stress runs at seq=512/1024 on the L4 pool to estimate per-request RAM and KV size.
- int8 quantization smoke test with our standard calibration set; will compute perplexity and n-gram regression vs fp16.

Preliminary blockers / questions:
1) We need the customer's prompt corpus (Avery / CS) — small sample of ~200 prompts.
2) Which quantization profile should we test first? We have two common profiles: q8_eco and q8_lat. I recommend q8_lat for POC because of the latency requirement.
3) Do we allow automatic fallback to the eos-xs-mt-v1-quant variant if the allocator cannot meet p50 targets? (Jonas to confirm)

Attaching an initial allocation estimate: alloc-estimate-rt-8gpu.xlsx. I'll post results to the Drive folder and create a short runbook for the staging Canary.

-Dev

--
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Eos-XS-2.7B: adaptive pin & compat checks for CloudScale POC

Team — reviewed thread and attachments. Provisional approval for a temporary pin for the CloudScale POC (Nov 1–Nov 30) under the following conditions:

1) Telemetry contract: Dev to add token-level latency and error counters to the POC stream and expose dashboard for CS & Sales.
2) Canary: Start with 5% traffic in staging for 48 hours, then stagger to 25% if no regressions.
3) Rollback plan: Jira ticket JIRA-INF-1427 must be created with explicit rollback steps and an on-call roster.
4) Fallback policy: We will allow automatic fallback to eos-xs-mt-v1-quant only if latency spikes >3x p50 and after CS approves customer-facing notification.
5) Security/compliance: Priyom — confirm there are no data retention or encryption flags for CloudScale (they requested audit logs).

If Dev can confirm the three runs (tokenizer, KV-stress, quant smoke) by EOD Thu, we'll lock the provisional pin and notify Sales to confirm with CloudScale.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Model Governance & Ops
Redwood Inference
